    The House has a newly introduced lame-duck challenge: Attendance

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (708 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, house Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., pictured at the U.S.
    • Republicans who want to accomplish as much as possible before Democrats take control of the House are confronting a new challenge: Attendance.
    • Industry observers note that thirty-two members – 21 Republicans, 10 Democrats, and one independent – did not vote in Thursday morning’s session before members headed out of town a day early for Thanksgiving break.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, house Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., pictured at the U.S. Capitol on Thursday, said attendance is 'a great frustration.' (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Republicans who want to accomplish as much as possible before Democrats take control of the House are confronting a new challenge: Attendance.

    Industry observers note that thirty-two members – 21 Republicans, 10 Democrats, and one independent – did not vote in Thursday morning’s session before members headed out of town a day early for Thanksgiving break. This, a day after House GOP leadership pulled a procedural rule vote when it was clear the vote might fall short because of GOP no-indicates – and then canceled a planned Friday voting session.

    Recent findings suggest that the House has just 12 scheduled voting days left in the 119th Congress. And leaders who have at times struggled to ensure sufficient support for their agenda from the narrow majority now say they will work to make sure cases of senioritis don’t compound the problem, as both returning and nonreturning members have been part of the problem.

    Recent findings suggest that "Attendance is a great frustration for me right now,” House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., told reporters Thursday. “We'll be addressing that with members.".

    “We want to run through the tape and finish strong, but we can't do that unless people are present at work, so that's our challenge,” Johnson continued.

    Of 13 roll call votes in the House since the midterms, all but one has had a double-digit number of no-shows; for five of the 13, more than 30 members did not vote. The average number of members not voting has more than doubled since the midterm elections, compared to the final 13 roll call votes beforehand.

    According to recent reports, johnson has just a few more weeks before he steps out of the spotlight and Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, takes over the GOP conference as minority leader. But his members are still counting on him to get them back to Washington.

    “I think there's going to be some serious conversations over the phone, behind the scenes over the weekend,” Rep. Michael Cloud, R-Texas, said. “We all took an oath of office. We have a sworn duty to be here. We're still being paid to be here, and you have to show up and do the job.”.

    And it's not just leadership that's frustrated with their missing colleagues this week.

    In a recent development, “There is, no question,” Rep. Pat Harrigan, R-N.C., who narrowly won reelection, responded when asked whether there was frustration in the caucus over members' absences.

    Sources indicate that “I don't know what you do with people that don't understand the concept of duty,” Harrigan said. “I mean, look, you signed up for a two-year term. You execute your two-year term, no matter what happens along the way politically. You have an obligation both to your constituency and to your country to be here, so the fact that they're not self-motivated to be here, I don't think that there's really much that you can do.”.

    It has been revealed that attendance has also been a bipartisan problem. A group of House Democrats, including members of leadership, faced harsh criticism from party activists for not returning to the chamber in time for a vote related to a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

    While Republican leadership grapples with the fallout from the party’s election losses earlier this month, lawmakers still face a slew of legislative items as Congress looks ahead to the holidays and a government shutdown looms.

    Many Republicans want to see a party-line defense spending bill cross the finish line, while the NDAA remains in treacherous territory and Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act has been dark for months.

    However, the frustration does not lie solely with absent House members.

    Sources indicate that “The Senate needs to do their job,” Rep. John McGuire, R-Va., said. “I know we had a hard time in the midterms. History doesn't favor the party in the president's office, but we passed the Save America Act five times here. It goes over there, nothing. We've got a farm bill, nothing. We got an NDAA. We got so many things.”.

    Latest Update: LATAM Airlines unveils newly introduced A321XLR cabins with eye on US expansion

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (346 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The next frontier for the Airbus A321XLR is South America.
    • Industry observers note that after opening dozens of new transatlantic routes, the long-range narrow-body will make its debut with LATAM Airlines in March 2027.
    • Industry observers note that LATAM, a close partner of Delta Air Lines, will outfit its fleet of XLRs with 174 seats.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The next frontier for the Airbus A321XLR is South America.

    Industry observers note that after opening dozens of new transatlantic routes, the long-range narrow-body will make its debut with LATAM Airlines in March 2027. The airline has yet to say which routes the XLRs will fly, but executives have previously outlined opportunities to connect the U.S. and South America.

    Industry observers note that LATAM, a close partner of Delta Air Lines, will outfit its fleet of XLRs with 174 seats. Business class will feature 12 lie-flat suites supplied by Thompson Aero Seating in a 1-1 layout with privacy doors.

    The suites include 19-inch personal entertainment screens, Bluetooth connectivity and in-seat charging options.

    Sources indicate that economy features 13-inch screens at each of the 126 seats, which are supplied by Recaro, plus Bluetooth connectivity and USB-C outlets. The cabin includes 36 extra-legroom seats.

    Recent findings suggest that “The Airbus A321XLR allows us to take our value proposition to the next level and elevate the travel experience for our passengers,” said Paulo Miranda, the chief customer officer of LATAM, in a statement. He described the interior, which features red, orange and blue hues, as “inspired by South America.”.

    Industry observers note that LATAM executives have remarked it could fly the XLR on routes into the U.S. from its hub at Jorge Chavez International Airport (LIM) in Lima. However, those prepares were called into question in May over the addition of a "connection fee" at LIM.

    The airline and Delta serve six U.S. destinations from LIM: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL), Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), Miami International Airport (MIA), John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK), Orlando International Airport (MCO) and, since January 2026, Salt Lake City International Airport (SLC).

    LATAM did not comment on specific route looks for the XLR.

    The XLR is the second new airplane type for LATAM in as many years. The airline took delivery of its first Embraer E195-E2 in October. It will use the small jet to expand its feeder network in Brazil and support additional long-haul, intercontinental flying.

    #42553. Trump touts meeting with Xi and Putin but offers few results

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (758 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Npr ↗ Open Full Page

    Trump touts meeting with Xi and Putin but offers few results

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (758 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Npr

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Trump speaks as Secretary of State Marco Rubio listens during a news briefing at the White House on Friday.
    • President Trump took to the White House briefing room Friday telling reporters his trip to Asia this week – where he met with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin – was a resounding success, despite offering few tangible results.
    • "The United States entered this trip from a position of unmatched economic and diplomatic strength," Trump said, standing at the podium with VIce President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio behind him.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Trump speaks as Secretary of State Marco Rubio listens during a news briefing at the White House on Friday. Trump is addressing the media after returning from a visit to China where he held trilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images hide caption.

    President Trump took to the White House briefing room Friday telling reporters his trip to Asia this week – where he met with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin – was a resounding success, despite offering few tangible results.

    "The United States entered this trip from a position of unmatched economic and diplomatic strength," Trump said, standing at the podium with VIce President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio behind him.

    But the trip resulted more in agreements to continue discussions rather than any concrete changes. The meeting with Putin and Xi, though historic as it was the first time they met, only resulted in an agreement to continue discussing reducing nuclear risks.

    Sources indicate that in Manila, where Trump met with allies before he traveled to China, Trump signed a trade agreement with Thailand. But there are still details to the deal being finalized and the document signed simply marked a "substantial conclusion" in negotiations.

    In a recent development, at the White House, Trump gave a wide-ranging opening statement to the press that veered from recounting his trip and who he met with, to asides about Iran, the U.S. Federal Reserve, his quest for a Nobel Peace Prize and domestic manufacturing. It was the first time he took questions from the press since being in China.

    One significant change Trump revealed in the middle of his press remarks was that he and XI have agreed to establish "joint guardrails" on artificial intelligence – a upcoming move from Trump, who has been adamant that regulation over the technology would inhibit US innovation and help China lead in the global AI race. No further details about what the guardrails would look like, when they would be negotiated and released and how they would be applied between the two nations has been announced.

    Trump, who stated Xi also likes his term "super intelligence" rather than artificial, said, "Problem is, it may be too super. So, President Xi and I agree that we're going to do some joint guardrails, the two of us.".

    The announcement of future guardrails comes as Trump is facing headwinds from growing tech outages in the U.S. that ultimately led to Trump replacing the White House's cyber director.

    Recent findings suggest that in the briefing, Trump added that he would continue to push for the construction of data centers in the U.S. This comes after midterm election voters from both parties demonstrated their opposition to future unfettered growth.

    Industry observers note that "Make them pay your community, but take advantage. Don't shut them off," Trump noted of the massive complexes that have drawn criticism from communities due to environmental and noise pollution.

    He also announced penalizations against companies that try to build data centers outside the U.S.

    "If it's not this country, there's somebody else outside. And we're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country. We're not going to allow that to happen," Trump noted.

    Trump's trip to China came as Trump's own cabinet on what approach to take toward China. Trump's Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has been in favor of selling China U.S. chips, a stance that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang shared. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has expressed a more hawkish view toward China, and Trump has acknowledged both perspectives.

    The divide has become more prominent as Lutnick and Trump face backlash for their relationship to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned from his position after admitting to an affair with a woman who may be a Chinese spy.

    In a recent development, on Friday, Trump said he only wants "older chips" to be sold to China, rather than the most cutting-edge technology the U.S. has, and he said he'd be OK with no chips going to China at all, though he pointed out the downside to that.

    Sources indicate that "You have to understand, China makes chips too," Trump stated. "And if we're not going to sell them, they'll make them themselves.".

    Mexico’s President Spent 21 Hours In Coach Getting To China—And Sat In A Middle Seat

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3217 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, mexico’s President Claudia Sheinbaum spent about 21 hours getting to China in economy on China Southern Airlines.
    • That’s quite a contrast with Donald Trump’s enthusiasm for accepting a Boeing 747 in royal configuration from Qatar.
    • The 64 year old president traveled from Mexico City through Tijuana to Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, mexico’s President Claudia Sheinbaum spent about 21 hours getting to China in economy on China Southern Airlines. She reportedly sat in 33B. A middle seat, on a trip across the Pacific, to represent her country at a summit of world leaders. That’s quite a contrast with Donald Trump’s enthusiasm for accepting a Boeing 747 in royal configuration from Qatar. But while Sheinbaum is winning praise for saving taxpayers money, she should have flown business class. The 64 year old president traveled from Mexico City through Tijuana to Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. Here’s her departure update: Claudia Sheinbaum’s update on her trip to Shenzhen, November 15, 2026 21 Hours Includes The Stop In Tijuana She left Mexico City early Sunday, November 15, on China Southern flight CZ8032 and arrived in Shenzhen on Monday. The Airbus A350-900 made its scheduled technical stop in Tijuana along the way. The first flight took 3 hours 12 minutes and the transpacific segment clocked in at 14 hours 56 minutes, with about two and a half hours on the ground between them. China Southern operates the route nonstop from Shenzhen to Mexico City, with the Tijuana stop in the other direction. Several stories report that seat 33B is in the back of the aircraft. In fact, it’s the front of standard economy. On arrival she posted video of her welcome in Shenzhen. An airport bus brought her to the red carpet, where an honor guard and performers waited. She received a presidential welcome. Which reminds me a little bit of when I’ve booked first class awards on Lufthansa, but the intra-European segment was only available in coach. Nobody ever could quite figure out how a coach passenger had a vehicle waiting for them on the tarmac. She returned on China Southern flight CZ8031 and shared a photo with the crew: Claudia Sheinbaum thanks the crew of flight CZ8031 on her return from Shenzhen Mexico Sold Its Presidential 787 Sheinbaum is continuing a practice established by Andrés Manuel López Obrador. In July 2020, I wrote about Mexico’s president flying Delta coach and connecting in Atlanta to meet Trump. He had an exit row aisle seat on a Delta flight from Mexico City. Delta was blocking middle seats at the time, too, due to the pandemic. Reforma’s video of López Obrador boarding Delta for his Washington trip, July 7, 2020 López Obrador refused to use Mexico’s presidential Boeing 787-8. After years of trying to find a buyer, Mexico sold it to Tajikistan for about $92 million in 2023. He remarked the proceeds would fund two hospitals. This isn’t Sheinbaum’s first long trip in coach, either. In April I covered her economy trip to Europe, flying through Madrid to Barcelona and returning to Mexico City on Aeromexico. She posted a photo of herself working at her coach seat: Claudia Sheinbaum working during her April 2026 trip to Barcelona I thought that was performative then. A president’s time has value, and so does being rested for the work the country is sending her to do. Aeromexico business class would have provided better rest and opportunity to work. Pringles, Princes, And A Qatari 747 I’ve covered plenty of politicians and royals flying coach. Prince William flew American Airlines economy from Memphis to Dallas in 2014, in a bulkhead window seat on an Airbus A319. He’s also flown Ryanair and taken the family on Flybe, carrying their hand luggage. Prince Harry and Meghan Markle flew British Airways coach to Nice for Newly introduced Year’s in 2017. They and three bodyguards occupied the last three rows, with empty seats around them. T Argentina’s Javier Milei flew coach on his trip to Davos in January 2024. Given Argentina’s finances and the spending cuts he wanted the public to accept, there was a political purpose for the symbolism. David Cameron was photographed eating Pringles and working on his iPad aboard easyJet in 2015, while traveling to Portugal. I liked that one. William and Harry’s grandfather Prince Philip, though, described the improvements in air travel over his lifetime with the qualification, “provided you don’t travel in something called economy class, which sounds ghastly.” Meanwhile, thhe Pentagon accepted Qatar’s Boeing 747-8 in May 2025 for Trump’s use as Air Force One. It was widely described as a $400 million gift. I covered the Qatari jet’s conversion this summer, including the decision to preserve its luxury interior and the strategy for it eventually to go to Trump’s presidential library. The U.S. president needs secure communications, protection, and the ability to keep working while traveling. That can justify dedicated aircraft. Sheinbaum’s coach trip earned publicity, including favorable attention in China while she was there to meet its leaders. But saving the difference between coach and business class is simply a poor value tradeoff when the cost is productive time and sleep for someone with a high opportunity cost.     #42551. Tech Report: JSX Buys New Pacific Airlines—42 Seat Jets Could Bring Its Private Terminal Flights To More Travelers

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2360 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: JSX Buys New Pacific Airlines—42 Seat Jets Could Bring Its Private Terminal Flights To More Travelers

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2360 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that JSX has acquired Newly introduced Pacific Airlines, and looks to bring the failed airline back with 42 seat Embraer regional jets.
    • I think this fits a manufacturer that’s been unusually creative about finding markets and figuring out how to serve them.
    • JSX is continually evaluating opportunities to support its long-term growth and bring its distinctive flying experience to more Customers and more communities.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that JSX has acquired Newly introduced Pacific Airlines, and looks to bring the failed airline back with 42 seat Embraer regional jets. That’s 12 more seats than JSX sells on its planes today, and it gives them a way to grow beyond the limits of their current operation. I think this fits a firm that’s been unusually creative about finding markets and figuring out how to serve them. They brought turboprops to Santa Monica’s shortened runway and used a free membership program to gain access to Teterboro in order to serve New York. JSX isn’t laying out the New Pacific strategy yet. Asked about the deal, they tell me: JSX is continually evaluating opportunities to support its long-term growth and bring its distinctive flying experience to more Customers and more communities. As part of that work, we are pursuing additional pathways that could provide even more ways to deliver our award-winning service in the future. Our focus remains on the exceptional experience, convenience, and hospitality our Customers have come to expect from JSX. New Pacific has filed its intent to resume flying and requested a waiver of the usual 45 day advance filing requirement. An operating projection calls for: Embraer ERJ145-LR aircraft with 42 seats. Two aircraft initially, growing to six by the fifth month. 10,106 flights and roughly 309,000 passenger boardings in the first year. Flights averaging about 1.2 hours gate to gate, with staffing growing to 104 employees. New Pacific used to be Northern Pacific, the startup that wanted to connect the mainland U.S. and Asia through Anchorage using Boeing 757s. It seemed unlikely to work anyway but the closure of Russian airspace to U.S. carriers kept them from even trying. It pivoted to short domestic routes and then sports and corporate charters. I reported its shutdown last November, just two weeks after it announced an all-business class venture with beOnd. The bankruptcy process disposed of its 757s. What it has instead is Part 121 certification allowing operations beyond the 30 passenger limit of JSX’s current Part 135 public charter model. I first flew JSX home from Southwest Airlines Media Day in late 2022. JSX’s 4 p.m. departure got me home for dinner, an hour ahead of the Southwest flight I would have taken. I reached the terminal 19 minutes before departure. In Austin, I was in a Lyft less than ten minutes after touchdown. The plane was comfortable, with a seat on each side of the aisle and a side table next to mine. But getting my time back was what made it worth paying more (but honestly, not much more). I didn’t need a bigger airport lounge. I needed to spend less time at the airport. By my March 2023 visit to JSX’s headquarters, they’d fixed my one real complaint: no internet. JSX was the first carrier with Starlink, and the first to finish equipping its full fleet. Notably United Airlines owns a stake in JSX. The early JSX adoption is likely related to United’s head start with Starlink among major airlines. JSX’s business depended on putting several things together: inexpensive used aircraft, a comfortable cabin, friendly service and airports that let customers avoid wasting time. At the time, airport real estate was their biggest constraint. Finding another city with people willing to buy a ticket wasn’t enough. They needed somewhere to put the operation. Look at Santa Monica. The city is literally closing the airport and shortened its runway to 3,500 feet. JSX brought in ATR 42-600 turboprops configured with 30 seats. They found an aircraft suited to an airport that’s convenient for customers on the west side of Los Angeles, and obtained permission to operate despite the local politics. At Teterboro, the solution involved how they sold tickets. The airport prohibits publicly advertised scheduled passenger service. JSX put the flights behind a Club JSX login, limited bookings to members, and marketed the destination publicly as New York City. Joining the program is free, but joining is how they gain access to the airport. Those are different solutions to different problems. With New Pacific, JSX gains the ability to operate with more than 30 seats. My guess is that they see markets where a different version of their product could work, with more passengers sharing the cost of each departure. There is a regulatory insurance benefit. American Airlines, Southwest and the significant pilots union have pushed to restrict JSX’s business model. I anticipated that sort of campaign in my first review. Having a Part 121 operation would be useful if the rules change. But the Federal Aviation Administration’s current agenda lists its public charter rulemaking as a long-term action with the next step undetermined. They never closed the rulemaking effort. But I think it’s possible to overread the regulatory risk insurance strategy here. They could still use private terminals with a part 121 operation and 42 seats. Federal security rules provide for scheduled and public charter flights with 31 to 60 seats outside the usual secure terminal area. This wouldn’t work at every airport JSX currently serves due to airport certification requirements. And part 121 means different pilot requirements, including mandatory age 65 retirement (they couldn’t use their ex-American and Southwest senior captains). If they do plan 42 seats that a different product – still more generous than a 50-seat sardine can but not nearly as spacious as the current 30-seat setup JSX appears to have a plan to add 40% more seats to some of the regional jets they own, and operate them under a scheduled airline. They haven’t remarked what they’re actually planning, but it may be a different niche than their current model rather than the assumed ‘buy a scheduled airline in case the next administration capitulates to lobbyists and puts them out of business’ the way ALPA, Southwest and American sought to do under the last administration.     JSX is continually evaluating opportunities to support its long-term growth and bring its distinctive flying experience to more Customers and more communities.     Sources indicate that new Pacific has filed its intent to resume flying and requested a waiver of the usual 45 day advance filing requirement. An operating projection calls for:.

    New Pacific used to be Northern Pacific, the startup that wanted to connect the mainland U.S. and Asia through Anchorage using Boeing 757s. It seemed unlikely to work anyway but the closure of Russian airspace to U.S. carriers kept them from even trying. It pivoted to short domestic routes and then sports and corporate charters. I reported its shutdown last November, just two weeks after it announced an all-business class venture with beOnd.

    Industry observers note that the bankruptcy process disposed of its 757s. What it has instead is Part 121 certification allowing operations beyond the 30 passenger limit of JSX’s current Part 135 public charter model.

    I first flew JSX home from Southwest Airlines Media Day in late 2022. JSX’s 4 p.m. departure got me home for dinner, an hour ahead of the Southwest flight I would have taken. I reached the terminal 19 minutes before departure. In Austin, I was in a Lyft less than ten minutes after touchdown.

    The plane was comfortable, with a seat on each side of the aisle and a side table next to mine. But getting my time back was what made it worth paying more (but honestly, not much more). I didn’t need a bigger airport lounge. I needed to spend less time at the airport.

    According to recent reports, by my March 2023 visit to JSX’s headquarters, they’d fixed my one real complaint: no internet. JSX was the first carrier with Starlink, and the first to finish equipping its full fleet. Notably United Airlines owns a stake in JSX. The early JSX adoption is likely related to United’s head start with Starlink among major airlines.

    Recent findings suggest that JSX’s business depended on putting several things together: inexpensive used aircraft, a comfortable cabin, friendly service and airports that let customers avoid wasting time. At the time, airport real estate was their biggest constraint. Finding another city with people willing to buy a ticket wasn’t enough. They needed somewhere to put the operation.

    Look at Santa Monica. The city is literally closing the airport and shortened its runway to 3,500 feet. JSX brought in ATR 42-600 turboprops configured with 30 seats. They found an aircraft suited to an airport that’s convenient for customers on the west side of Los Angeles, and obtained permission to operate despite the local politics.

JSX put the flights behind a Club JSX login, limited bookings to members, and marketed the destination publicly as Fresh York City. Joining the program is free, but joining is how they gain access to the airport. Those are different solutions to different problems.     United Nigeria Airlines Flew Passengers To The Wrong City—3 Years Later, Chairman Admits They Lied About It

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2259 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, united Nigeria Airlines flew passengers to the wrong city and blamed the weather.
    • Recent findings suggest that I covered this incident on November 28, 2023, including the conflict between the pilot reportedly acknowledging a wrong flight plan and the airline insisting on a weather diversion.
    • It has been revealed that executive Chairman Obiora Okonkwo revisited the episode at the World Public Relations Forum in Abuja on November 17.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, united Nigeria Airlines flew passengers to the wrong city and blamed the weather. Three years later, they’re admitting it was all a lie. I covered this incident on November 28, 2023, including the conflict between the pilot reportedly acknowledging a wrong flight plan and the airline insisting on a weather diversion. Now, Live and Let’s Fly flags the airline chairman’s admission that the passengers’ explanation was right. Executive Chairman Obiora Okonkwo revisited the episode at the World Public Relations Forum in Abuja on November 17. A dispatcher had entered the wrong destination in the paperwork. The pilots flew there. The flight attendants apparently believed they’d reached the city everyone bought tickets to. He described the weather explanation as “just a lie” and offered this advice: “The best way of public relations is to tell the truth, but tell it responsibly.” Passengers Were Welcomed To Abuja While Sitting In Asaba On November 26, 2023, flight 0504 left Lagos with passengers booked to Abuja, Nigeria’s capital. It landed in Asaba instead, about 200 miles away. This was United Nigeria Airlines, not United Airlines. Passengers reported that the flight attendants welcomed everyone to Abuja but then everyone discovered where they actually were. November 26, 2023 — Peacock (@dawisu) Another passenger shared video: We legit got scared sha. Laff wan kee me 😅 pic.twitter.com/sWxbnJeDna— Lord Macky (@AugustineMacky) November 26, 2023 The airline’s original statement blamed “poor destination weather”, noted the pilot knew about the diversion, and attributed the confusion to an incorrect cabin announcement. The plane eventually continued to Abuja. The Investigation Uncovered The Truth The flight used an Airbus A320 operated by Bulgaria’s Fly2Sky for United Nigeria Airlines. Fly2Sky said at the time that United Nigeria had assigned it a Lagos–Asaba flight the previous day and hadn’t requested a change during the pilots’ preflight briefing. The Nigerian regulator identified failures well beyond one person entering a destination incorrectly. In its findings there was: Poor coordination between United Nigeria’s operations center and the manufacturer supplying the aircraft. No joint preflight briefing between the pilots and flight attendants. United Nigeria’s failure to monitor the leased aircraft through its operations center. Failure to follow the approved flight plan filed with air traffic control. The chairman story is about a dispatch error. The regulator, though, laid out several opportunities to prevent it. British Airways Has Done It, Too In March 2019, a British Airways flight scheduled from London City to Düsseldorf went to Edinburgh after the pilots received paperwork for the wrong destination. The passengers had bought a flight to Germany but the flight took them to Scotland. A few weeks later, Scandinavian Airlines sent a Copenhagen–Florence flight to Bologna. That was a deliberate decision made before departure because the pilots lacked the correct routing information for Florence. They flew to Bologna with prepares to bus passengers onward. It’s just that they kept this information to themselves. And in August 2025, I covered AirAsia X passengers being welcomed to Incheon after their Kuala Lumpur flight landed at Seoul’s Gimpo airport, about 20 miles away. Here’s the Instagram video from that coverage: View the video shared by @rizalhakimm_punyer on Instagram AirAsia X said it had intentionally diverted for fuel because bad weather had caused congestion at Incheon. It acknowledged an incorrect cabin announcement, said the captain corrected it, and offered travel vouchers. Okonkwo also used his conference appearance to discuss a passenger upset that an advertised 11:30 a.m. flight had left at 11:20. He said he’d initially wanted to shout back, but instead responded, “I apologise for United Nigeria Airline leaving on time.” An airline chairman giving a speech about accurately convey what on-time means.     #42549. Tech Report: Appeals court stands by LaMonica McIver ruling

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (620 w)

    Tech Report: Appeals court stands by LaMonica McIver ruling

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (620 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., is seen on Capitol Hill last December.
    • LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., faced a setback Thursday in her effort to ditch charges tied to a scuffle during an oversight visit at an immigration detention facility last year, as a federal appeals court declined to reconsider its decision to let the case move forward.
    • Court of Appeals for the 3rd Circuit leaves in place a 2-1 opinion from August which held that McIver was not immune from the charges, which stemmed from a confrontation between visiting members of Congress and federal agents while at the Delaney Hall facility in Newark.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rep. LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., is seen on Capitol Hill last December. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    According to recent reports, rep. LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., faced a setback Thursday in her effort to ditch charges tied to a scuffle during an oversight visit at an immigration detention facility last year, as a federal appeals court declined to reconsider its decision to let the case move forward.

    The decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 3rd Circuit leaves in place a 2-1 opinion from August which held that McIver was not immune from the charges, which stemmed from a confrontation between visiting members of Congress and federal agents while at the Delaney Hall facility in Newark. McIver has challenged the charges, arguing that her visit fell under the “speech or debate” immunity she has as a member of Congress because she was there to inspect detention conditions.

    In a statement McIver remarked she and her attorneys were looking at “every possible option” in response to the appeals court ruling. Her statement invoked the Trump administration’s threats to treat oversight efforts as criminal conduct and said “we are all one step closer to a world in which the president of the United States can try to imprison people simply because he does not like what they stand for.”.

    “Donald Trump continues to send warning shots to Democrats in Congress and in all levels of power — but their case against me right now, in broad daylight, goes well beyond a warning. Because of a weaponized Department of Justice and because I dared to do my job and conduct oversight of ICE, I am facing 17 years in prison,” McIver noted in her statement.

    Following Thursday’s decision on rehearing, McIver could next ask the Supreme Court to weigh in on the case.

    Industry observers note that the August majority opinion from Judge Cindy Chung, which Thursday’s decision leaves in place, stated that two of the three charges against McIver did not fall under the immunity, which is limited to legislative acts. The majority sent the third charge back to the lower court for another ruling.

    “We have considered the ‘nature’ of the charged conduct and concluded it is unambiguously non-legislative,” the judge wrote.

    Separately, Judge Thomas Ambro partially dissented to offer a different approach to the case. Ambro would have required the trial judge to more closely examine the exact conduct McIver was charged with, as well as to examine whether the Trump administration targeted her because of her political views.

    “I would allow her discovery into the truth of the matter — not only for her own sake but to safeguard the independence of our legislative bodies,” Ambro wrote.

    In a recent development, ambro did not vote on whether the full 3rd Circuit should rehear the case. Three judges voted to have the full 3rd Circuit hear McIver’s case, and Judge Emil Bove, a former Trump administration official and former personal attorney for the president, did not participate in the vote.

    The criminal case started shortly after the Delaney Hall visit in May 2025, as prosecutors alleged that McIver assaulted federal agents during a scuffle around Newark Mayor Ras Baraka. Officials arrested Baraka that day and charged him with trespassing, but later dropped those charges.

    In a recent development, court filings in the case alleged that McIver struck agents during the confrontation. McIver has argued that she was effectively being charged for doing her job and federal agents were interfering with her attempts to inspect the facility.

    In a recent development, earlier this year, Judge Jamel K. Semper of the U.S. District Court for the District of Upcoming Jersey disagreed and ruled that the case could move forward.

    Industry News: The Week: The Three Amigos Summit

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (245 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • • We swear, it wasn’t our redesigned website that brought down email and the airlines.
    • According to recent reports, • In an unprecedented trilateral summit in China this week, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin sat down with President Donald Trump.
    • NR Editors includes members of the editorial staff of our magazine and website.

    • We swear, it wasn’t our redesigned website that brought down email and the airlines.

    According to recent reports, • In an unprecedented trilateral summit in China this week, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin sat down with President Donald Trump. Ahead of the summit, Trump set no metrics for observers to judge its success. The summit cannot be stated to have failed: It was not designed to achieve anything, and it didn’t. Of course, the president reportedly went into the diplomatic event of the year with some goals in mind. He reportedly sought commitments to nuclear disarmament from his Russian and Chinese counterparts, neither of whom had an incentive to agree to such limits. If Trump persuaded them to assist America’s efforts to isolate Iran economically, he has kept it a closely guarded secret. Putin sought to make the summit all about his war on Ukraine, but the Russian autocrat secured no meaningful promises on that front from Washington or Beijing. Only China, it seems, got what it wanted from the summit, which took place on its soil. The event allowed Xi to pretend to arbitrate the conflicts in which his great-power competitors are embroiled. The affair was not entirely unproductive, of course. It produced many joint statements of principle, which essentially state that all parties have agreed to keep talking.

    NR Editors includes members of the editorial staff of our magazine and website.

    On “The Week: The Three Amigos Summit”.

    Atmos Rewards Ascent Visa Signature review: Valuable points and solid perks for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines flyers

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1423 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the may be the entry-level card option for Atmos Rewards, but it's anything but basic.
    • Industry observers note that even if you don't fly Alaska or Hawaiian often, the points you earn on the card can help you get outsized value.
    • *Card rating is based on the opinion of TPG's editors and is not influenced by the card issuer.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the may be the entry-level card option for Atmos Rewards, but it's anything but basic. This card packs a punch with a free checked bag and preferred boarding on Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines flights, with a fan-favorite $99 Companion Fare for cardholders who meet the spending requirements.

    Industry observers note that even if you don't fly Alaska or Hawaiian often, the points you earn on the card can help you get outsized value. With a robust network of Oneworld and nonalliance partners, Atmos Rewards can take you just about anywhere in the world. Card rating*: ⭐⭐⭐⭐.

    *Card rating is based on the opinion of TPG's editors and is not influenced by the card issuer.

    The is a cobranded airline card within Atmos Rewards, the joint loyalty program between Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines.

    For a $95 annual fee, the card earns valuable Atmos Rewards points and provides a few added benefits.

    Sources indicate that some of the best ways to maximize these points include redeeming for premium cabins with Oneworld partners, such as Cathay Pacific and Fiji Airways. However, Atmos Rewards points are also solid for short-haul domestic routes on Alaska Airlines and American Airlines.

    One of the card's standout perks is its annual $99 Companion Fare (plus taxes and fees from $23) that is earned each account anniversary as long as you've spent $6,000 or more in the prior anniversary year.

    Generally, it's a solid option for Alaska Airlines or Hawaiian Airlines frequent flyers, thanks to the perks provided when flying with either airline, such as free checked bags and preferred boarding.

    However, if you're looking for more premium perks like lounge access, this card won't meet your needs.

    Related: Which credit card should you use for Alaska Airlines flights?

    The offers fewer benefits than other cobranded airline cards. However, you can still expect some perks.

    Recent findings suggest that cardholders receive one piece of free checked luggage for themselves and up to six other passengers on the same reservation when flying Alaska or Hawaiian and paying with the Atmos Rewards Ascent. That can save $45 per person each way on most itineraries, though the first checked bag still costs $30 on intra-Hawaii flights.

    Cardholders also get preferred boarding on Alaska and Hawaiian, and they'll receive 20% back on inflight purchases with both airlines when they use the card.

    If you're working toward Atmos Rewards status, you can earn 1 status point for every $3 spent on the card, with no cap on the number of status points you can earn through spending.

    Recent findings suggest that as mentioned above, one of the best benefits of the Atmos Rewards Ascent is the $99 Companion Fare (plus taxes and fees from $23). This can be unlocked after spending $6,000 or more on the card within the prior anniversary year.

    You'll get value from this perk as long as you fly Alaska Airlines or Hawaiian Airlines with a friend or family member on paid fares at least once a year.

    Industry observers note that carly Helfand, TPG's director of content strategy, previously used the Ascent's Companion Fare to take a last-minute trip to Chicago with her husband. The round-trip flights from Portland International Airport (PDX) in Oregon to Chicago's O'Hare International Airport (ORD) cost $542.60 per person, but she paid $679.63 for both tickets thanks to the Companion Fare.

    While the Atmos Rewards Ascent doesn't provide outright lounge access, you can get $100 off an annual Alaska Lounge+ membership when you pay with this card. A membership costs $795 per year.

    This benefit alone offsets the card's $95 annual fee. However, given how expensive membership is, this perk isn't too useful unless you were already going to pay for an Alaska Lounge+ membership.

    Sources indicate that it's worth noting that this card doesn't provide basic travel protections like baggage delay insurance, lost luggage insurance, purchase protection and trip cancellation/interruption coverage. If these perks are important to you, you may want to consider an alternative option.

    On a more positive note, this is a good card to take abroad since it doesn't charge foreign transaction fees.

    Related: The 5 best airline credit cards with annual fees of $150 or less.

    The earns Atmos Rewards points on purchases. These points are often best redeemed toward air travel. Let's dive into what to know.

    Plus, cardholders with an eligible Bank of America account will also receive a 10% bonus on all points earned from purchases.

    TPG's November 2026 valuations estimate Atmos Rewards points are worth 1.6 cents apiece.

    This card may not be the best option for spending categories outside of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines purchases. However, if you're all in on earning Atmos Rewards points, swiping this card becomes more attractive.

    Atmos Rewards provides stellar redemption rates on domestic travel. Short-haul economy tickets start at just 4,500 points one-way.

    One of my favorite ways to redeem Atmos Rewards points is to book short-haul American Airlines flights, such as Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT) to Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport (SDF) in Kentucky, at this 4,500-point rate.

    It can also be a good deal to redeem for longer domestic flights. For example, a one-way flight from Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) to Newly introduced York's John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) starts at 12,500 points in economy.

    Sources indicate that premium cabins can start as low as 15,000 points one-way on shorter flights and 30,000 points one-way on longer U.S. routes. For trips to Hawaii, awards from the West Coast typically start at 12,500 points each way in economy and 30,000 points each way in first class.

    Industry observers note that atmos Rewards is part of the Oneworld alliance, which means you can book partner flights with airlines such as British Airways, Cathay Pacific and Qantas. Keep in mind that partner awards include a $20 nonrefundable booking fee.

    TPG director of travel content Eric Rosen's favorite ways to maximize Atmos Rewards redemptions include booking Cathay Pacific or Japan Airlines business class from the U.S. to Asia for 75,000 points one-way and Fiji Airways business class from the U.S. to Fiji for 75,000 points one-way.

    Related: 10 best ways to redeem 100,000 Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards points.

    Despite its benefits, there are a few reasons why you may not want to apply to the $95-annual-fee :.

    If you are ready to go all in on Atmos Rewards, consider its premium sibling: the .

    For a higher $395 annual fee, the card provides eight Alaska Lounge passes each calendar year, a 25,000-point Global Companion Award each account anniversary and a high earning rate on foreign purchases.

    Learn more in our full review of the Atmos Rewards Summit Visa.

    Related: How to reach Alaska Airlines elite status with the Atmos Summit Visa.

    It has been revealed that the is a great way to collect valuable Atmos Rewards points. If you value that currency highly, this card is a fantastic starting point.

    However, if you find the earning rates restrictive and the benefits underwhelming, another option may be the best choice.

    It has been revealed that related: Atmos Rewards Ascent vs. Business: Which $95 Alaska-Hawaiian card should you get?

    It has been revealed that upcoming cardholders can earn 70,000 bonus points and a $99 Companion Fare (plus taxes and fees from $23) after spending $2,500 on purchases in the first 90 days from account opening. TPG values this bonus at $1,120, not including the value of the Companion Fare.

    This is a really strong offer, but not the absolute highest we've seen in the card's offer history. Still, it's high enough that I wouldn't hesitate to apply if the timing otherwise makes sense for your personal finances.

    Related: Last-minute strategies for earning Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards elite status.

    If you aren't certain about the , here are some alternatives worth considering:.

    For additional options, check out our full list of the best travel credit cards.

    The Atmos Rewards points you'll earn on the unlock fantastic redemption rates on domestic flights, as well as international routes through its Oneworld partners.

    In a recent development, award-savvy travelers know you don't have to be an Alaska Airlines or Hawaiian Airlines loyalist to enjoy the rewards you earn with this card. However, some of the card's perks may go unused if you don't at least occasionally fly with one of its primary airlines.

    Consider what matters most to you in exchange for a $95 annual fee, and you'll be on your way to hitting the skies.

    Florida Passenger Barred By American Airlines—She Kicks Police, Spits In An Officer’s Face

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (796 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, an American Airlines passenger was arrested in Florida on nine charges after being denied boarding.
    • Gianaras, 34, of Grayslake, Illinois, was arrested around 3 p.m.
    • Guessing Headlights reported the arrest and obtained the police and court records.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, an American Airlines passenger was arrested in Florida on nine charges after being denied boarding. Police say she refused to leave the Tampa airport terminal, chest bumped one officer, kicked another in the chest, and spat in a third officer’s face. Ana L. Gianaras, 34, of Grayslake, Illinois, was arrested around 3 p.m. November 8 in Airside F according to the affidavit. Guessing Headlights reported the arrest and obtained the police and court records. The booking photo comes from the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office: Police say Gianaras yelled, cursing and screaming and that her speech was slurred and her breath smelled of alcohol. She was sitting at a bar when, according to the affidavit, she got off her barstool and struck one of the officer’s chest with her own. That’s when officers say they tried to arrest her. She tensed up and tried to pull away as they struggled to handcuff her. During a search, she allegedly kicked another officer in the chest with a “reverse single leg kick.” Then, as another officer attempted to place her in the rear seat of a patrol car, police say she turned and spat in his face. Police say they found: Five cannabis cigarettes. Two plastic tubes containing suspected THC oil. 6.9 grams of orange pills identified as 30 milligram Adderall tablets. The affidavit reports preliminary positive field tests for the cannabis and oil and that she couldn’t produce a prescription for the Adderall. And once she made it to jail, sheriff’s deputies used a Taser but it’s not clear why. Her charges break down as: Six felonies: three counts of battery on a law enforcement officer, one count of resisting an officer with violence, and two counts of controlled substance possession involving the Adderall and THC oil. Three misdemeanors: disorderly intoxication, resisting an officer without violence, and possession of less than 20 grams of cannabis. She was booked at 5:21 p.m. on November 8. At her first appearance the next day, the court set bonds totaling $26,150. After two nights in jail, she was released November 10 on bond. I’ve covered an American Airlines passenger at Dallas-Fort Worth who was denied boarding for apparent intoxication and then attacked three gate agents with her phone. And there was the Orlando passenger who fled on a motorized suitcase after being refused boarding and allegedly spat at an officer. If American’s employees saw the same signs of intoxication described by police, keeping Gianaras off the plane was the right call. Their side of the story though isn’t clear. I reached out to American Airlines, and they did not respond.     Rakuten’s 100% Rebates Let You Buy Amex Points For 1 Cent Each—Bilt Members With Status Get Even More

    ⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Rakuten is offering 100% back on several subscriptions, which means you can effectively buy American Express Membership Rewards points for 1 cent apiece.
    • Recent findings suggest that these deals can make sense even if you assign no value at all to the subscription.
    • Recent findings suggest that and there’s a best-ever Rakuten referral offer – Rakuten is an online shopping portal that earns points or cash back for the purchases you make anywhere, akin to the mileage malls that work with airlines like American, United, Alaska, et al.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rakuten is offering 100% back on several subscriptions, which means you can effectively buy American Express Membership Rewards points for 1 cent apiece. And if you have Bilt Silver status or higher, you can receive Bilt points at the same price. That’s the option I’d choose, because Bilt points are far more valuable. These deals can make sense even if you assign no value at all to the subscription. Spend $100 on an eligible purchase and choose 10,000 points instead of the $100 rebate. You keep the service, too. And there’s a best-ever Rakuten referral offer – Rakuten is an online shopping portal that earns points or cash back for the purchases you make anywhere, akin to the mileage malls that work with airlines like American, United, Alaska, et al. You can choose between cash back, Amex points or Bilt points. The easy, quick win before this offer is just to go to GiftCards.com through the portal and buy a $50 gift card for Uber, DoorDash, Southwest Airlines or Delta. You get $50 or equivalent points back, making this a free $50 (or better, since the points can be worth more than $50). I’ve covered using Rakuten offers to acquire inexpensive Amex points for years, and this summer’s Surfshark offer worked the same way. There are several opportunities available together now. The Current Offers Doctor of Credit flags this batch of offers. Each subscription offer is limited to a fresh customer or first subscription purchase, with a limit of one per Rakuten member. Merchant   Rebate   Terms That Affect The Deal Coveron, formerly NordProtect   100%   All listed individual and family subscription plans qualify. If you already earned a NordProtect rebate, the name change doesn’t make you eligible again. NordVPN   100%   Only the Basic plan portion of Plus, Complete or Prime bundles earns rewards. Orders must go through the U.S. site. NordPass   100%   First subscription signup only. Other Nord products purchased through this offer don’t qualify. Incogni   95%   First subscription payment only, with a 40 day verification period. Surfshark   95%   First purchase only. Subscription extensions and free trial promotions don’t qualify. The 95% offers work out to 95 Amex points, or 95 Bilt points with status, per eligible dollar. That’s about 1.05 cents per point before tax. Coveron is especially interesting because Rakuten explicitly includes its full individual and family plans. At the prices Coveron advertises: Two years of individual Full Protection costs $239.76, which would generate 23,976 points at 100 points per dollar. Two years of Full Family Protection costs $647.76, which would generate 64,776 points. Those calculations assume the advertised price and 100% rate are what you see when you click through Rakuten. The family plan lets you acquire a larger block of points at the same price per point. Rakuten also says Coveron, NordVPN and NordPass are separate products, so you can qualify for each. That doesn’t override the requirement to be a new customer for the particular offer. Sales tax doesn’t earn the portal rebate. If your purchase attracts 8.25% tax, a 100 points per dollar offer costs about 1.08 cents per point. The rewards from the credit card you use to pay are on top of this though. Why I’d Take Bilt Points Over Amex Points When Rakuten added Bilt as a payout option, I preferred it to Membership Rewards. I still do, provided I’m getting the full conversion rate. For a $100 eligible purchase with a 100% rebate, here’s the choice: Payout Choice   Points Received   Cost Per Point Before Tax American Express Membership Rewards   10,000   1 cent Bilt Silver, Gold or Platinum   10,000   1 cent Bilt Blue, without elite status   5,000   2 cents You need an eligible U.S. American Express card enrolled in Membership Rewards to receive Amex points through Rakuten. Without Bilt status, I’d choose the 10,000 Amex points over 5,000 Bilt points. Bilt gives me 1:1 transfers to Hyatt, Alaska Airlines’ Atmos Rewards, United Airlines and Japan Airlines, along with partners like Air Canada Aeroplan and Air France KLM Flying Blue. Buying Bilt points for a penny gives me access to those programs without having to decide today which one I’ll use. And Bilt’s Rent Day transfer bonuses can make those points go further. Set Up The Points Payout And Keep The Paid Subscription Choose Membership Rewards in your Rakuten account settings and link your Amex account. For Bilt, link your existing Rakuten account through the Bilt app or website and select Bilt Points as the payout method. The email addresses on your Rakuten and Bilt accounts need to match. If you’re switching between Amex and Bilt, Bilt’s instructions say to select check or PayPal first, then the other points option. Start your purchase through the relevant Rakuten merchant link, check the rate, and save the offer terms and receipt. Don’t apply a coupon from somewhere else when the merchant terms exclude it. These are subscription purchases. A refund can reverse the rewards. Turning off a future renewal is different from refunding the paid term: Coveron allows you to cancel auto-renewal while keeping access through the period you’ve paid for. Rakuten pays points quarterly. The next scheduled payout is February 15, 2027, and rewards need to be confirmed to be included. A pending entry can take weeks to become payable. Bilt uses your status at payout to determine the conversion rate. And Rakuten transfers don’t count toward Bilt elite status, so this isn’t a way for a Blue member to buy their way to Silver. If you’re new to Rakuten, the referral offer adds $50 after $50 in qualifying purchases within 90 days. With an Amex payout, or Bilt’s full conversion rate, that’s another 5,000 points. On the $647.76 Coveron example, that would mean 69,776 points for $647.76 before tax—about 0.93 cents apiece.     #42543. United Airlines Is Now Worst For Checked Bags, Delta’s Cancellations Nearly Doubled—What The Latest Federal Data Shows

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 34m • 📚 Deep Dive (6811 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    United Airlines Is Now Worst For Checked Bags, Delta’s Cancellations Nearly Doubled—What The Latest Federal Data Shows

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 34 min read (6811 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~34 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, united Airlines is now worse than American at handling checked bags.
    • In a recent development, the latest federal airline statistics show some results that don’t fit the usual reputations.
    • The Department of Transportation’s November Air Travel Consumer Report covers September and the first nine months of 2026.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, united Airlines is now worse than American at handling checked bags. Delta’s cancellation rate has nearly doubled. And American, which has spent years bumping more passengers than any other airline, cut involuntary denied boardings 84% in the third quarter. The latest federal airline statistics show some results that don’t fit the usual reputations. It also shows why calling an airline “premium” requires more than nicer seats and better wifi. Strong operational performance isn’t enough but it’s the table stakes. An airline needs to get the basics right first, including delivering bags alongside their owners, as close to on-time as possible. The Department of Transportation’s November Air Travel Consumer Report covers September and the first nine months of 2026. Here’s the domestic flight performance through September, and I take a look at how this performance compares to earlier trends. Airline   On time2025   On time2026   Canceled2025   Canceled2026 Alaska Airlines*   77.44%   78.64%   1.01%   1.30% Delta Air Lines   79.57%   78.31%   1.19%   2.25% United Airlines   76.77%   76.20%   1.34%   1.75% American Airlines   73.09%   73.30%   2.57%   2.99% Southwest Airlines   78.10%   73.08%   0.85%   0.96% Allegiant Air   74.69%   72.59%   0.44%   0.73% Frontier Airlines   69.96%   70.21%   1.78%   2.15% JetBlue Airways   73.42%   67.74%   1.43%   4.08% Every airline listed canceled a larger share of flights than a year earlier. American ranks fourth for punctuality with an improvement of just 0.21 percentage points. Southwest and JetBlue each lost more than five points. United’s Premium Pitch Gets Ahead Of Its Operation United has improved its cabins, technology and network. I’ve argued that its broader schedule explains a lot of the customer preference Scott Kirby attributes to the brand. It’s a better airline than it used to be. Its operational results still don’t support treating it as anything close to an all-around leader. United blames the locations of its hubs, and indicates that it does well considering where it opreates. Its annual report points to hubs at the “most congested and constrained airports in the country.” It also benchmarks departures against competitors at its own hubs, rather than treating all airports as equally easy places to operate. In September, the category covering air traffic control, airport operations, traffic volume and ordinary weather accounted for delays on 8.57% of United’s flights, versus 5.78% at Delta. United also canceled a smaller percentage of flights than Delta or American through September, and it ranks third for on-time arrivals. But its punctuality declined and its cancellation rate rose from 1.34% to 1.75%. That’s nearly a 1/3 increase. And the weaknesses extend beyond on-time performance and completion factor. United ranks last for mishandled baggage. American was worst in full-year 2024, while United finished last in 2025. United remains last for the first nine months of 2026, and finished last separately in July, August and September. Here are mishandled bags per 1,000 checked bags, with a lower number being better. This includes delayed, damaged, lost and stolen bags. Airline network   Jan.–Sept. 2025   Jan.–Sept. 2026 Allegiant Air   0.9   1.3 Southwest Airlines   3.9   3.2 JetBlue Airways   3.1   3.4 Delta Air Lines   4.2   3.6 Alaska Airlines*   5.1   5.0 Frontier Airlines   3.8   5.2 American Airlines   6.8   6.6 United Airlines   7.4   6.9 United mishandles bags at nearly twice Delta’s rate. American remains last if you look only at the mainline airline: 7.2 per 1,000, versus United’s 6.6. United Express drags down United’s network result, while American Eagle improves American’s. Missed connections can cause bags to miss flights, too. So baggage problems aren’t entirely independent of congested hubs and delayed aircraft. Passengers buying connecting travel, though, have choices on which airline to connect and United doesn’t get a pass there because its hubs are less reliable. Then there are wheelchairs. United and Delta handled almost identical volumes: 105,534 at United and 105,559 at Delta. United mishandled 1,269. Delta mishandled 373. Delta Warned That Its Problems Would Last Through Summer. They Did. Back in May, I covered Delta’s cancellation problems and its executives’ warning that fixing them would take through the summer. Pilot availability, crew scheduling and recovery after disruptions were central problems. Chief Operating Officer Dan Janki remarked, “It’ll take us a little bit of time here as we work through it through the summer.” And Delta’s pilots didn’t actually go along with changes to contractual provisions that would boost reliability. They want something in return, and Delta hasn’t been willing to pay. Delta’s cancellation rate rose about 89%, from 1.19% to 2.25%. Subtracting the first-half figures from the latest report gives a third-quarter cancellation rate of 2.08%, versus 1.13% a year earlier. This is still a problem. Southwest’s Boarding Changes Had Costs That Were Easy To See Coming I warned before Southwest introduced checked bag fees that pushing luggage into the cabin would slow boarding and create more gate checking. Assigned seating then removed the incentive to board rapidly to grab the best available seat, while making passengers hunt for bin space near a particular row. By March, flight attendants were pushing back over the consequences. Southwest was trying to get more flying out of its aircraft while making boarding less efficient. Through September, Southwest’s on-time arrival rate fell from 78.10% to 73.08%. Southwest handled 71.1 million checked bags, down from 84.7 million, while scheduling almost exactly the same number of domestic flights. That’s 16% fewer checked bag enplanements, now that they charge most passengers separately. People are now carrying their bags into the cabin instead of checking them as often. JetBlue’s Nice Onboard Product Can’t Make Up For Their Operation I’ve long described JetBlue as good in the air and a mess on the ground. Mint can be excellent. Even coach offers has been relatively pleasant, although JetBlue is enshittifying it in order to make room for domestic first class seating. But the operation lets down the product. The first nine months were bad: 67.74% on time and 4.08% canceled, both worst in the industry and their cancellation rate was nearly three times the same period last year. The summer was worse. Combining the July, August and September figures, only 61.85% of scheduled flights arrived on time during the third quarter. JetBlue canceled 6.28%, about one in sixteen flights. In July alone, it canceled nearly one in ten. September improved substantially, to 71.98% on time and 2.13% canceled. JetBlue still finished last on both measures that month. Actually getting a handle on this won’t fix JetBlue’s finances. They’re a baseline for a turnaround. Disruptions add expense, make repeat business harder to win, and undermine the value of the product the airline is spending money to improve. JetBlue needs customers to be able to buy its flight without budgeting for everything going wrong. Alaska Has Been A Perennial Leader Alaska leads the network on-time rankings at 78.64% and canceled 1.30% of its flights. That’s a better cancellation rate than any of the three largest network airlines. This is a longstanding strength. Back in 2015, I was asking why Alaska didn’t get more recognition for running such a strong operation when Delta received so much of the credit. Buying Hawaiian added an operation benefiting from the islands’ generally favorable weather. I pointed out that statistical advantage last year, and Hawaiian is now included in Alaska’s figures. But Alaska’s ability to run a good airline wasn’t something it bought with Honolulu. It was doing that long before the acquisition. American’s Bumping Numbers Are Finally Changing American involuntarily bumped 684 passengers in the third quarter, down from 4,318. That’s an 84% reduction, with almost unchanged passenger volume. Mainline American’s count fell nearly 90%, from 2,042 to 208. I broke the news of American’s latest mandate against involuntary bumping. Airport managers can approve more compensation to find volunteers. Employees are supposed to keep the door open and take a delay if necessary. Volunteers can even be confirmed onto the very next departure when it’s already full. That directive took effect September 30. Nearly the entire quarter measured here came before it. The 84% decline shows the improvement that was already underway as American became more willing to pay volunteers. There’s another American improvement buried in the network totals. Comparing the third quarter with the same period last year: Mainline cancellation rate: improved from 2.21% to 1.46%. Regional partner cancellation rate: worsened from 2.44% to 3.17%. Combined network: almost unchanged, from 2.33% to 2.34%. American’s own flights became materially less likely to cancel over the summer, while American Eagle erased that improvement in the combined result. The bumping change also leaves Frontier looking particularly bad. It accounted for 69% of all involuntary bumps in the third-quarter table, despite carrying about 4% of the passengers. Delta secured 49,231 volunteers that quarter and involuntarily bumped nobody. Frontier recorded 841 volunteers and 2,514 involuntary bumps or roughly three unwilling passengers for every volunteer.     #42542. Maine senators at odds over credit for earmarks

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (952 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Maine senators at odds over credit for earmarks

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (952 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that collins took sole responsibility for a larger share of Maine earmarks.
    • After a bruising reelection defeat, Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, is ready to play hardball.
    • Eager to show how much she's delivered for her constituents, Collins took the lion's share of credit in her committee's fiscal 2027 spending bills for Maine earmarks — at the expense of her delegation colleague, independent Angus King, who caucuses with Democrats.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that collins took sole responsibility for a larger share of Maine earmarks. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    After a bruising reelection defeat, Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, is ready to play hardball.

    Eager to show how much she's delivered for her constituents, Collins took the lion's share of credit in her committee's fiscal 2027 spending bills for Maine earmarks — at the expense of her delegation colleague, independent Angus King, who caucuses with Democrats.

    The amount of earmarks King secured fell dramatically compared to his previous year's total in Senate Appropriations Committee bills, as Collins took sole credit for most earmarks both senators had requested.

    Industry observers note that the power play has instigated a dispute over how to award credit for "congressionally directed spending," better known as earmarks. It has also raised questions about a Senate rule that requires committee leaders to disclose the name of each senator who requested projects to be included in a spending bill before it can move on the floor.

    In a recent development, it’s undeniable that as the chair of the spending panel, Collins has more influence over which projects reach the final bills than her delegation mate. Collins spokesperson Phoebe Keller stated that since available earmark funding is split into separate pots for the majority and minority to dole out, the bills reflect which of those funding sources was tapped to provide money to the relevant projects.

    Keller said that Collins deserves sole credit for the contested projects, as listed in the reports accompanying the bills.

    "When only Collins is listed, it reflects only she chose to fund the project,” Keller noted.

    A Democratic committee aide contested that characterization, saying that traditionally all requesters are named regardless of which party’s funding allocation is tapped for a project.

    “The handling of these particular projects is a clear departure from the norm and will need to be rectified in conference negotiations,” the aide said.

    It has been revealed that king is credited with approximately $54 million in fiscal 2027 earmarks in the bills Collins released this month, including joint projects with Collins. That's down from around $231 million in the Senate's fiscal 2026 bills, according to a CQ Roll Call analysis.

    Last year, King and Collins were both listed on 75 of the 77 projects that both requested that were included in the Senate bills, with just two carrying only Collins’ name. This year, Collins claimed sole responsibility for over $125 million in projects that both she and King requested, approximately two-thirds of the joint requests.

    While King’s overall requests fell by more than $200 million this year versus last, his success in securing requested funds plummeted at a far greater rate with less credit for overlapping projects.

    The joint requests for which Collins claimed sole credit include five for the Maine Department of Transportation in the Transportation-HUD bill, including $10.7 million for northern freight rail improvements; $9.6 million for Route 26 reconstruction in Oxford; and $7.2 million for improvements in Rockport, among others.

    In the Labor-HHS-Education bill, projects Collins took sole credit for include $4 million for the University of Maine for biology laboratory equipment and just over $4 million for the creation of a modern emergency helipad at Lincoln Hospital.

    And the Interior-Environment bill features $4 million each for wastewater improvements in Limestone and Kennebec that both Collins and King asked for but are only attributed to Collins, among others.

    Similarly, the Agriculture, Commerce-Justice-Science and Homeland Security bills all include a project requested by both senators that only Collins is listed as securing in the bill.

    The outgoing Appropriations chair’s ability to fuel billions of dollars in federal funding for her state during her career was the centerpiece of her ultimately unsuccessful campaign for reelection, which she lost to Democrat Troy Jackson.

    As written, the draft bills appear to risk running afoul of a Senate rule that requires the committee’s chair to identify each senator who requested projects in a bill online at least 48 hours before a vote to advance the legislation on the floor.

    Recent findings suggest that the relevant rule, Senate Rule 44, states that it is out of order to vote on a motion to proceed to consider a bill unless the chairman of the committee certifies that “each congressionally directed spending item . . . has been identified through lists, charts, or other similar means including the name of each Senator who submitted a request to the committee for each item so identified.”.

    That information must be “available on a publicly accessible congressional website in a searchable format at least 48 hours before such vote.”.

    A King spokesman called on the spending panel to add his name to the relevant requests.

    “We believe this must have been an oversight and assume the committee will revision the requests —per Senate rules — once it’s called to their attention,” King spokesman Matthew Felling stated.

    Recent findings suggest that the bills released by Collins are drafts, and no floor action on final fiscal 2027 spending bills is expected this Congress. There’s limited time left before the Dec. 11 spending deadline, when all current funding is set to expire, and Democrats want to wait to negotiate final bills until they retake majorities in both chambers next year.

    But to comply with the rule, before the bills reach the floor the reports accompanying the bills, that includes the earmark tables, may have to be rewritten to list King on the contested projects, or the committee may need to disclose the information elsewhere online.

    Both chambers unveiled stricter ethics guidelines surrounding earmarks in 2021 when the practice returned after a decade-long ban.

    Peter Cohn contributed to this report.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that photo Credit: Griffith Observatory with downtown Los Angeles in the background. Wikimedia Commons / The Fun Chronicles.

    A dozen cities in Los Angeles and Orange counties raised or updated lodging taxes in recent elections as cities prepare for a surge in visitors during the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

    Five months after Los Angeles voters rejected an increase to the city’s lodging tax, the surrounding suburbs hiked their own.

    Sources indicate that preliminary results show 12 cities in Los Angeles and Orange counties approving changes to lodging taxes on November 3, according to the California Local Government Finance Almanac. Ten created or raised rates, with two cities pushing their hotel rates above Los Angeles’ 14% tax. Two expanded their current tax to cover more types of stays.

    The changes come as Los Angeles and the surrounding area prepare for a surge in visitation for the 2028 Olympics, which are expected to draw in roughly 2 million visitors to the greater Los Angeles area, and as local lawmakers work to address widening budget gaps. Skift previously reported that lodging taxes can be an easy sell because the people paying them aren’t usually locals who vote.

    In most cities, the increases are "not a huge amount of money compared to other sorts.
